sensors.name: Account kiosk
sensors.description: The touchscreen where riders sign in, check a balance, or reset a PIN. It is the front door to an account, and attackers knock on it first.

foundAt.summary: In the public concourse of every station, before the fare gates.

manufacturers.quirk: ISO timestamp string and loud SCREAMING_SNAKE keys. You parse a date before you can do anything.
Epoch milliseconds, and the failure reason hides in a second field. 'declined' plus reason 'pin' means wrong PIN.

sensors.name: Fare gate
sensors.description: The turnstile that guards the paid area. A tap either opens it or does not. It is the Z0 to Z1 boundary in physical form.

foundAt.summary: At the paid-area boundary of every station.

manufacturers.quirk: Direction is the word ENTRY or EXIT, result is PERMIT or REJECT, and the card is a MEDIA_SERIAL.
Balance is in integer cents, not currency units. 250 here is not 250, it is 2.50.
Everything is a code. Line 3 means red, d:1 means in, rc:0 means ok. You need the lookup table to read a single event.

sensors.name: Ticket vending machine
sensors.description: The machine that sells fares, tops up cards, and issues refunds. It handles money, so it draws fraud like a picnic draws ants.

foundAt.summary: In the public concourse of every station.

manufacturers.quirk: The only maker of this sensor, so at least it is consistent. Amounts in cents, transaction type in UPPERCASE, card as a mediaToken.

sensors.name: Door reader
sensors.description: The badge reader on a staff or restricted door. It decides who crosses from one trust zone into the next.

foundAt.summary: On every door between zones Z1 and Z4, at stations, depots, signal cabins, and the control center.

manufacturers.quirk: The badge holder is CARD_HOLDER, the decision is GRANTED or DENIED, and the zone is bare like Z4 with no lowercase.
Sentinel calls a door a PORTAL and a site a FACILITY, so its location codes never line up with Gatekeep's. Decision is ALLOW or DENY.

sensors.name: Door contact sensor
sensors.description: The magnetic sensor that reports whether a door is open, closed, forced, or propped. It watches the door itself, not the badge.

foundAt.summary: On the same doors as the readers, at stations and staff sites.

manufacturers.quirk: The event is a number. 0 close, 1 open, 3 forced, 4 held. A forced door reads as ev:3 and nothing more.
Spells the state out as FORCED_OPEN or HELD_OPEN, but glues two ideas into one field, so 'forced' and 'open' arrive together.

sensors.name: Platform camera
sensors.description: The camera over a fare gate that counts bodies against grants. It turns a picture into two numbers: how many taps, how many people.

foundAt.summary: Above the fare gates of every station.

manufacturers.quirk: Grants is gr and people is px. Two letters, no explanation, and easy to swap by accident.
Verbose and clear, but the counts are GRANT_COUNT and PERSON_COUNT while RailSense uses gr and px. Same reading, opposite spelling.

sensors.name: Train tracker
sensors.description: The trackside sensor that logs a train arriving at or leaving a station, and on which track. It is the pulse of the moving system.

foundAt.summary: Along every line, at platforms and on the operational tracks.

manufacturers.quirk: Line is a numeric code again, and the event is a short string. Consistent with RailSense gates, which is the one small mercy.
Every key is romaji. jikoku is time, ressha is train, rosen is line, eki is station, idou is the movement. Precise, and unlike anything else on the wire.

sensors.name: Control console
sensors.description: The dispatcher's console in the control center. It logs every command sent to a signal, switch, or data store. This is the most sensitive telemetry in the system.

foundAt.summary: Only on the control floor of the Operations Control Center.

manufacturers.quirk: Clear enough, but the operator is OPERATOR and the console is CONSOLE, while Tetsudo names the same two things in romaji.
tantosha is the operator in charge, tanmatsu is the terminal, meirei is the command, taisho is the target. A dictionary is required.

sensors.name: Network relay
sensors.description: A node on the control backbone that links a station to the control center. It reports which host talked to which destination, and how many bytes moved.

foundAt.summary: At every station and staff site, on the network that carries departure boards, signals, and staff traffic.

manufacturers.quirk: Source is SRC_HOST, destination is DST_ADDR, and the byte count is BYTES_OUT. Long keys, easy to misread under load.
kyoten is the site, soshin is the source, atesaki is the destination, baito is bytes. Romaji again, so the two relay vendors share no key at all.
